findings.claim: The loop-7 per-row handling of malformed paths gives a placeholder-specific message for every path that is not a legal URI, so a row with a space in its path is told to replace a {placeholder} it does not have. send() (lines 265-272) turns any IllegalArgumentException from java.net.URI.create into MalformedRow, and row() reports it as 'write a real path, with an actual id in place of any {placeholder}'. URI.create throws for any string that does not parse as a URI, and a space is the commonest such case. Critic run at 505af8efafc0a91f276f379bf9f3a44da9dfb195, my own edit of the completion's step 6 rows: a validation row whose path appends an SQL-style condition with spaces to a booking id got that placeholder message, although the path has no braces. The step's own framing invites such a row: the reading pairs validation with 'bad input' (artifact.md line 30), and an injection-style string is the textbook example of bad input. A learner who did connect validation to bad input is given a reason that does not match what they wrote. Rows with literal {id} placeholders correctly got the message, each on its own row. Low, because the first clause, 'write a real path', is still the right action and a learner who removes the spaces then gets a true message from the row.

evidence.section: row(), lines 225-237 (message at line 232); send(), lines 265-272 (URI.create wrapped into MalformedRow)
create(String): any URISyntaxException from parsing is wrapped in an IllegalArgumentException

findings.recommendation: Make the message cover every cause URI.create rejects, for example: 'write a real path: an actual id instead of any {placeholder}, and no spaces (percent-encode anything an attacker would send)'. Or report a placeholder only when the path contains a brace, and use a separate 'this path is not a valid URI (does it contain a space?)' message otherwise. Rerun one row with a {placeholder} and one row with a space; each should get a message that names its own cause.

findings.claim: The loop-7 registration fix models in shipped, 'complete' code the hand-written controller validation that this lab tells learners does not count. AuthController.register (lines 27-38) now checks for a null or blank username or password with if-statements in the handler and returns 400 itself. The class Javadoc says it is complete and not edited, and README line 26 lists it as complete. Yet Task 7 step 3 (README line 110) asks for 'a Bean Validation constraint', the troubleshooting row at README line 192 says 'a hand-written check in the controller does not count', and the course's Bean Validation page teaches this exact case with @NotBlank on a request record and @Valid on the @RequestBody parameter, which turns a blank field into a 400 through MethodArgumentNotValidException. Validation is one of the five practices #o3 asks the learner to connect to its risk, and step 6 makes the learner read the login side of AuthController (its login helper posts to /auth/token). A learner who compares the two controllers sees the shipped model do what the lab forbids. Behaviour is correct (critic probe test on a completed copy: blank password, missing password and blank username each returned 400), so this is a modelling problem only. Low.

evidence.section: register, lines 26-38 (hand-written null and blank checks at lines 28-31); class Javadoc 'This class is complete; you do not edit it.'
line 26 (AuthController complete), line 110 (Task 7 step 3, Bean Validation constraint), line 192 (a hand-written check in the controller does not count)
Teaching: @NotBlank on a request record, @Valid on the @RequestBody parameter, MethodArgumentNotValidException becomes 400
Validation: Bean Validation applied to an @RequestBody parameter annotated with @Valid raises MethodArgumentNotValidException

findings.recommendation: Express the blank checks as Bean Validation: put @NotBlank on the Credentials record components and @Valid on register's @RequestBody parameter only, so /auth/token is unchanged and the 409 duplicate check stays in the handler as a business rule. Then rerun the probe (blank, missing and whitespace fields give 400; duplicate gives 409; new name 201) and the step 6 completion. The technology SME should confirm that the 400 body Boot then returns reveals nothing internal. If the hand check must stay, add a one-line comment saying why it is not Bean Validation, so the shipped code does not contradict README line 192.

items.note: Checked at 505af8efafc0a91f276f379bf9f3a44da9dfb195. lab.json still declares common-api-security-risks-owasp#o3, and Task 7 step 6 still carries it: for each of the five practices the objective names (validation, DTOs, error bodies without internals, password hashing, role checks) the learner writes the attacker request that practice answers, and task7ShowsTheAttackEachPracticeStops sends it to the finished app and judges it from runtime behaviour. Critic runs this round on fresh git-archive copies of 505af8efafc0a91f276f379bf9f3a44da9dfb195 (JDK 25.0.5, Maven 3.9.16, offline, mvn -q -o test from starter/). The shipped starter ran 10 tests and failed exactly the 9 lab.json failingTests; defaultProfileSendsNoCorsHeaders passed. The private completion exited 0 with no output, and surefire reported 2, 1 and 7 tests, matching expected/test-summary.txt (about 11 s here). Wrong-answer variants, each my own edit of the step 6 rows on a completed copy, failed on the right row with a true message: a guessed (not stolen) admin password, an unknown account, an anonymous caller in the role row, the reading's DELETE on an admin path this API lacks, an anonymous or non-numeric id in the validation row, another customer's booking and the public workshop list in the DTO row, an anonymous request and an unmapped path in the safe-errors row. Correct alternatives passed: a stolen-table login as a customer, the other customer on the admin action, ADMIN with a negative id written in lower case with extra spaces, the other customer's own booking for the DTO, and a customer asking for a booking that is not theirs for safe errors. So the act is executable and a row passes only when its practice is what answers the request. I judge #o3 practised. The connection is made per practice, not per risk label; the risk names come in the collapsed read-after block. Two new low findings (-017 placeholder message for a path with spaces, -018 the shipped AuthController models hand-written validation) do not undo the act.

API2:2023 lists 'Uses plain text, non-encrypted, or weakly hashed passwords' (hashing as API2 holds).
